::: {.ctm-hero}

**ABOUT THE PROJECT**

# Bringing mathematics and programming together.

Computational Thinking makes sense of Mathematics
(CTM) is a collaborative European project
exploring how programming and computational
thinking can support university mathematics
education.

:::


::: {.ctm-section}

## Why CTM?

Programming and computational thinking have
become increasingly important in education,
research, and professional life.

However, their integration into university
mathematics education remains uneven.

CTM was created to help address this challenge
by connecting educational experience across
European universities and developing practical
resources for teaching and learning.

The ambition is simple: make it easier for
students to learn mathematics through
computation, and easier for educators to
introduce programming into their teaching.

:::


:::: {.ctm-section .ctm-section-light}

## Our Objectives

CTM was designed around three connected goals.

::: {.grid}

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4}

::: {.ctm-card}

### 01. Investigate

Identify challenges, needs, and effective
practices for integrating programming into
undergraduate mathematics education.

:::

:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4}

::: {.ctm-card}

### 02. Create

Develop accessible tutorials, exercises,
and mathematical projects that strengthen
computational thinking and programming skills.

:::

:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4}

::: {.ctm-card}

### 03. Connect

Support collaboration and the exchange
of educational resources between
universities across Europe.

:::

:::

:::

::::


::: {.ctm-section}

## From Research to Resources

The CTM project was designed to connect
educational research with practical
teaching materials.

### Understanding the Challenges

Surveys and interviews with students
and educators were planned to identify
needs, obstacles, and existing practices.

### Developing Tutorials

The project planned to develop
browser-based learning modules to
introduce programming and computational
thinking in a mathematical context.

### Creating Mathematical Projects

The project also aimed to develop
exercises and student projects that
connect mathematical theory to
computational applications.

### Supporting Teaching Practice

Another important area was exploring
how computational projects can be used,
evaluated, and assessed in
university teaching.

:::


::: {.ctm-section .ctm-section-light}

## Mathematics Education in the Age of AI

As generative AI became more widely
accessible, new questions emerged about
the relationship between programming,
mathematical understanding, and teaching.

Although generative AI was not a central
part of CTM's original objectives,
its growing influence provides an
important perspective on the future
of computational mathematics education.

[Explore AI & Education](ai.qmd)

:::


::: {.ctm-section .ctm-partners}

## A European Collaboration

CTM brings together five partner
universities from across Europe.

- **Lund University**, Sweden
- **Aalborg University**, Denmark
- **Technical University of Denmark**, Denmark
- **University of Oslo**, Norway
- **Ruhr University Bochum**, Germany

The collaboration is intended to support
the exchange of knowledge, experiences,
and educational resources across
institutional boundaries.

:::
